title: Kenny is visiting!
description:
Kenny Is Visiting

Kenny Warren (tp) · Jeremy Viner (ts) · Sandro Sáez (p) · Phil Donkin (b) · Nathan Ott (dr)

New York-based trumpeter Kenny Warren is visiting Berlin and joins forces with Sandro Sáez and Nathan Ott for a special quintet featuring Jeremy Viner and Phil Donkin.

Built around original compositions by Sáez and Ott, the music brings together five distinctive voices with a shared interest in open forms, rhythmic interplay and collective improvisation. The result is a highly interactive sound world in constant motion, shaped as much by spontaneous interaction as by the compositions themselves.

Kenny Is Visiting captures a particular constellation in a particular moment — music shaped by the encounter itself.

title: Bjørn Solli Quartet
description:
Bjørn Solli Quartet

Norwegian guitarist and composer Bjørn Solli brings together an exciting international quartet for an evening of inventive, swinging and highly interactive jazz at Donau115.

With a career spanning more than two decades, performances in over 30 countries, and collaborations with some of the most celebrated musicians on the international jazz scene, Solli is known for his melodic imagination, rhythmic sophistication and playful approach to improvisation.

Joined by Béla Meinberg on piano, Makar Novikov on bass and Jordan Dinsdale on drums, Solli presents a selection of fresh original compositions alongside carefully chosen jazz standards. Expect spontaneous interplay, unexpected twists and plenty of room for four distinct musical personalities to shine.

Line-up:

Bjørn Solli – guitar
Béla Meinberg – piano
Makar Novikov – bass
Jordan Dinsdale – drums

title: Matthieu Mazué “Turn of Events” feat Francisco Mela and Diego Hedez
description:
A new project initiated in New York City by pianist Matthieu Mazué, “Turn of Events” brings
together three musicians with strong and distinct musical visions, each widely recognized for their
exceptional improvisational talents. Alongside Mazué is drummer Francisco Mela, a major figure
on the contemporary jazz scene who has performed with McCoy Tyner and Kenny Barron, and
trumpeter Diego Hedez, a regular collaborator of bassist William Parker.

Together, they explore new sonic territories within a deliberately bassless formation — an artistic
choice that frees the piano from its traditionally codified harmonic role. This absence opens the
way to a more transparent sound and a lighter, freer approach to the instrument. The dialogue
between piano and drums becomes a central pillar — not only supporting the trumpet but also
redefining the piano’s traditional role as accompanist. The drums, in turn, unfold with remarkable
rhythmic freedom, shaping the contours of improvisation with flexibility and inventiveness.

title: Tal Mia Everything
description:
Mia Knop Jacobsen is an award-winning Danish musician, composer, and music producer renowned for her captivating vocals, innovative compositions, and dynamic productions. Over a career spanning more than a decade, Mia has garnered international acclaim for her unique fusion of genres, effortlessly blending modern jazz, contemporary pop, and electronic elements into a sound that is distinctly her own. As both a solo artist and a collaborator, she has toured extensively across South America, Asia, North America, and Europe, performing at prestigious festivals and venues including Jazz Open Stuttgart, Kennedy Center for Performing Arts, and Belgrade Jazz Festival.

Berlin-based singer-songwriter and guitarist Tal Arditi creates intimate, cinematic live
performances where acoustic songwriting meets ambient electronics. Using live looping, layered guitars, vocals, and subtle electronic textures, he builds immersive soundscapes in real time, turning each concert into a unique experience.

Following the release of his debut album Love Myself on Swiss label Mouthwatering Records, Tal is touring Europe with a show that moves seamlessly between delicate solo moments and rich, expansive arrangements. The album was launched with a sold-out release show at Kantine am Berghain and received extensive support from German media, including Album of the Week at WDR 3 Resonanzen and SR Kultur, alongside airplay and live sessions on Deutschlandfunk Kultur, FluxFM, Bayern 2, MDR Kultur, and rbb radioeins.

After touring with artists including Black Sea Dahu and Steph Strings, collaborating with members of The Rolling Stones, and performing at Sydney Festival, Tal continues to captivate audiences with performances that are both emotionally honest and musically adventurous.

title: FRIGO feat. Bruno Bode
description:
Somewhere along their search, the trio FRIGO begins to speak a musical language that follows its very own grammar. While drawing on avant-garde vocabulary from contemporary classical music and modern jazz, they never lose sight of form, expression – and thus, accessibility.
Their distinctive performance of original compositions explores polyrhythmic structures and extended harmony, providing a foundation for exciting improvisations full of surprising twists and vivid interplay. Their goal is to create striking moments of clarity, yet the music also thrives on the ambiguity born from their expanded approach to rhythm and harmony. Through their balanced acoustic sound, this polyphony ultimately converges into a singular, powerful musical expression – articulated with great intensity and sincerity.

title: Domingo Fantástico X with Antajayú and Isa Otoya
description:
I am pleased to present a new edition of Domingo Fantástico, the music and variety series held at Donau115. Inspired by the great weekend television shows that shaped generations across Latin America and Spain, this event celebrates diversity, creativity, and cultural exchange in Berlin.

This edition takes us from the roots of Andean music to contemporary explorations of Latin American music, bringing together two artistic approaches that combine tradition, experimentation and a personal perspective on sound.

Antajayú offers a musical journey through the Andes. Originally formed as a duo in Berlin and now a trio, the group combines violin and Andean instruments in a repertoire that brings together traditional folk music and original compositions. Their music also explores tango and Celtic traditions, with an energy close to rock. The name combines the words anta and ajayu, evoking the elements of earth and air. This duality reflects the dialogue between roots and new horizons that defines their sound.

Isa Otoya, a musical artist born in Lima and based in Berlin, has developed her own artistic voice as a singer-songwriter, composer and producer. Her music blends elements of Latin American traditions with electronic and pop sounds. After professional training in academic composition and singing in Peru, she moved to Europe in 2022 to study music production and sound engineering. She has independently produced two albums, De un Acorde (2021) and LLAR (2024), and is currently working on the post-production of her third album, scheduled for release in 2027. Her work spans songwriting, contemporary composition and instrumental pieces for interdisciplinary projects.

Another evening of music, stories, encounters and surprises at Donau115.

description:
Abura-Kadabura is the brand new rhythm duo formed by American drummer Dominick Gray and Argentine percussionist Zoe Wasinger.

Hidden pop structures form the basis of the interaction between Gray and Wasinger’s diverse sensibilities, using texture, dynamics, and a kinetic musicality to create unique songs drawing from the likes of Naná Vasconcelos, Airto Moriera, and Manu Delago.

title: TRYON
description:
TRYON is conceived as a living ensemble—one that brings together New York–based performers and improvisers to realise new and unreleased works composed in Berlin, Germany. At its core, the project seeks to create a dialogue between European experimental composition practices and the deep improvisational traditions of New York, with free improvisation serving as a foundational and unifying element.

TRYON will be performing music from their new upcoming album "Salmon Dreams". 
TRYON have released two albums on Double Moon Records. “Läuterung” which was released with a 13 piece ensemble in 2022 comprised of: Ganna Gryniva, Erik Leuthäuser, Omri Abramov, Toms Rudzinskis; and in 2023 “Freaky Squash Baby” which was released as an 18 piece group featuring: Kiki Manders, Mirna Bogdanovic, Erik Leuthäuser, Oli Steidle, Taiko Saito, Rieko Okuda, Philipp Gropper, Jasper Stadhouders, and many more.

TRYON has performed as both large and small ensemble versions in:

Jazzexzess, Jazzam Kaistersteg, VIllingen Jazzclub, Freakshow Artrock Festival, Ponava Jazz Festival, Improdimensija Concert Series, Nordhausen Jazzclub,  M//Darbnica, Kaunas Jazz Academy, Donau115, Bflat, Jazzclub Schlot, Terminus Saarbrucken, Saxstall, Kultūras nams Wiktorija, LOFT, and many more.

“Jazz rock and rock sounds and rhythms can at one point morph into jazz avant-garde or emotional and even tender statements. At other moments, the musicians play intellectually and sonically demanding or meet at a certain point on the level of the classic jazz form. There are no rules here. There is a wonderful, seemingly spontaneous game. You just have to listen to this album.”
Jazzfun.de

title: Feu Marinho
description:
Feu Marinho is a Brazilian singer, songwriter, and composer whose music blends Brazilian traditions, jazz, and oriental influences, shaped by themes of memory, movement, and human experience.

Joined by Malte Bogner, Yonatan Harari, César Belleyguier, Yannick Mäetelle and Nir Kleiner Feu is preparing to release his second album, Volume, in 2027. Co-produced by Feu,  Bogner, and Harari, the record expands his sound through rich arrangements and a collaborative creative process.

Having performed and toured across Europe, Asia, and Africa, Feu has developed an international presence through collaborations with artists from diverse musical backgrounds, including Jacob Collier, Daniel Harlev, Itay Spiegel, and Panda do Sol.

With Volume, Feu continues to explore the meeting point between cultures, composition, and improvisation, creating performances that move between intimacy and openness, shaped by the sounds and encounters that inspire his journey.

title: Florian Zimmer
description:
Florian Zimmer has been in a creative dialogue with artists in a variety of bands and duos in the course of the past three decades, including the long-running avant-hop trio Saroos alongside Christoph Brandner and Max Punktezahl, the industrial-punk project TVII SON, the dubwise duo Driftmachine featuring Andreas Gerth, and most recently his project Bella Wakame with prolific percussionist Andreas Haberl. Now the Berlin-based musician and composer is about to get even busier, this time as a solo artist. His improvised live sets draw on dub techniques and subtle grooves, mixing the sounds of his trusted modular synthesizers with a wide variety of samples to lysergic effect.

Zimmer straddles the line between abstract sound collaging and spontaneous live composition, utilising sounds from exotica or old educational records as well as field recordings to create ambiguities. Whether it is layered-and-looped polylogues between disembodied voices punctuated by melancholic melodica sounds, minimalist electronica, or intricate modular synthesizer rhythms that wouldn’t feel out of place on the dancefloor: Zimmer’s genre-transcending work with and around contrasts creates a sense of familiarity while evoking a feeling of uncanniness. The ever-changing interplay between sounds and rhythms, abstraction and concretion, semiotic serendipity and emotional warmth forms the dynamic and atmospheric core of his solo work.

title: Midori Hirano
description:
Midori Hirano is a Berlin-based Japanese musician, composer, and sound artist originally from Kyoto. Rooted in classical piano, she explores the space between structure and abstraction, acoustic and electronic sound. Her music builds layered soundscapes from piano, synthesizers, field recordings, and processed electronics, bringing the harmonic thinking of her piano background into experimental sound.

She has worked with a diverse range of artists, including string player Atsuko Hatano on Water Ladder (2021, Alien Transistor), Hprizm of Anti Pop Consortium (Love Control, 2017, raster), Brueder Selke on Split Scale (2025, Thrill Jockey), CoH on Sudden Fruit (2025, Ici d'ailleurs) and Ilpo Väisänen of Pan Sonic, with whom she has performed live. 

Her new solo album OTONOMA (February 2026) has been released on Thrill Jockey Records, followed by The Juniper Tree (October 2026), an album featuring her newly imagined score for Nietzchka Keene’s 1990 film of the same name, following its live premiere at Videodroom in Ghent in 2025. The album was released by VIERNULVIER Records, with the digital edition on Thrill Jockey Records.

title: Igor Osypov "Flying House"
description:
Igor Osypov presents his recent and most open-hearted project. Flying House opens a musical world with the unmistakable voice of guitarist Igor Osypov. The band presents a highly individual and immediately recognisable sound, balancing lyrical delicacy with dynamic rhythmic energy. The quartet’s subtle interplay and expressive depth create a sonic identity that is both distinctive and deeply memorable, leaving a lasting impression on the listener.

Flying House is a deeply personal upcoming album by guitarist Igor Osypov. In this music, Osypov dedicates each piece to the people and moments that shape his life—especially his family. The album focuses intentionally on the positive: cherishing the present, appreciating closeness, and finding warmth in the everyday.

Having spent much of his life as a refugee, escaping the reality of war, Osypov chose to center this project around a simple idea: living in the present. Flying House represents the feeling that home is not a fixed place but something that travels with the people you love. Wherever life takes you, home exists when those closest to you are near.

As a composer, Osypov returned to his most natural starting point: writing the music on his main instrument, the guitar. In this sense, the guitar becomes a metaphor for returning to one’s default setting, one’s musical home. While the guitar holds a central role in the sound of the album, the music leaves ample space for every member of the band to breathe, interact, and contribute their voice to the collective story.

Flying House is ultimately a celebration of presence, family, and the quiet joy of sharing music—and life—with the people who make any place feel like home.

Städtische Manieren
description:
Städtische Manieren (post-punk, experimental pop)
For fans of: Deerhoof, Sonic Youth, Suburban Lawns

Städtische Manieren are jumping in, head first!
Cheeky off-kilter guitars, massive walls of sound, the occasional freakout and stripped down
honesty, intertwined by a playfully expressive vocal – Städtische Manieren have created
inventive and challenging music that is hard to forget.

Blending 90s Alternative with modern Experimental Rock, Avant-Pop and a hint of Post-
Punk, they thrive on breaking and reshaping existing patterns and forms with a curiosity
reminiscent of bands like Deerhoof and Sonic Youth.

In their visceral live performances, audiences are caught up in the moment, ricocheting from
one sonic experience to the next. No safety net. No standstill. You want to dance, but you
don’t know how. Until you let go of everything you know and simply surrender to the
movement.

Städtische Manieren formed in Berlin around the end of 2022, with members Alda, Till, Enna,
and Till meeting in the context of Jazz. They soon scattered across Germany but continued
to work on the project, playing various underground venues and shaping the band’s sound.
In October 2025, their debut album Posterchild was released, a bold and colorful
introduction to the world of Städtische Manieren. Explosive yet introspective, it tackles
topics such as a culture of reflection without change, bottled-up anger and physicality,
showcasing their storytelling skills and intricate musicianship. Following the release, they played multiple shows in Germany, opening for acts like Lawn Chair and Andreya Casablanca, and are part of the lineup for About Pop and Fusion 2026.

title: Life is Great
description:
Bad Angles Pt.I Release Show

The German/Danish quartet returns in the form of a super limited EP Cassette Mixtape featuring six songs you can only physically own in this exclusive format. Wuuut? Sounds crazy but it’s true.
There’s no better way to enjoy the nostalgic compositions of bandleader/drummer Johannes Koch. Along with Asger Nissen’s passionate sax-noodlin’, Thorbjørn Stefansson’s warm, experienced bass, Johannes “Jojo” Mann’s bright, shimmering guitar and just a little extra synth for that perfect retro twist.

This mixtape features 3 brand new tracks, a live version, a swanky demo, and even a phat remix from Regensburg producer Jellysquash. It’s jazz that’s best enjoyed from the comfort of your cabrio: for best results, drive with the top down, and volume way up.

LIFE IS GREAT: A Berlin based up-and-coming quartet lead by drummer/composer Johannes Koch, and consists of  Johannes “Jojo” Mann on guitar,  bassist Thorbjørn Stefansson, and saxophonist Asger Nissen.  Compositionally, Koch recreates the feeling of his teenage indie/postrock - years, navigating between naive simplicity, rhythmic complexity and energetic improvisation. With music like this - the kind that makes you stop for a moment and reflect, and maybe even smile - then just maybe, life is not so bad after all.

Thomas MacMillan
description:
Thomas MacMillan is a composer and guitarist hailing from the remote Pennines region of Northern England. Now based in Berlin, he composes music for solo guitar inspired by horror films, liminal spaces, and video game soundtracks—creating an atmospheric soundscape that feels both familiar and unsettling.

On January 24th, he will perform his compositions at Donau115 for the first time. His repertoire includes pieces from his EP Negative Space—a concept album exploring liminal spaces and uncanny architecture—as well as his more recent release, Nervous System, an EP centered on anxiety, with each track delving into a different facet of this fundamental human emotion. His music evokes vivid, cinematic imagery while showcasing the impressive sonic range of the nylon-string guitar.

title: Ryan Blotnick / Jeremy Viner / Matthias Pichler / Joe Smith
description:
American guitarist Ryan Blotnick brings his “lyrical, textural, and tremulous” approach to Berlin with longtime collaborator Joe Smith (drums) and saxophonist Jeremy Viner.  His recent album The Woods has been hailed as “a mastery of hue and tone (Something Else!),” and compared to the John Abercrombie Trio with Dan Wall.  They are joined by the acclaimed bassist Matthias Pichler to present this music in Germany for the first time since the album’s release.      

Ryan Blotnick and Joe Smith met in Barcelona in the early 2000s. This led to tours with Pete Robbins, Bill McHenry, Bruce Arkin and eventually Blotnick’s debut album Music Needs You (Songlines) which featured Pete Robbins and Albert Sanz and came highly recommended by guitarists Ben Monder and John Abercrombie upon its release.

Blotnick and Jeremy Viner, both from Maine, have been collaborating mostly in the last few years, often performing with other artists who share Maine roots such as Mike McGinnis, Devin Gray and Mali Obamsawin.  

Praise for The Woods

“With this new album, the compelling textures created throughout speak to the group’s masterful work together.”

— Josh Gagnon, New York City Jazz Record

“Lyrical, textural, and tremulous, Blotnick's approach is painterly … The performances are characterized by restraint but in a manner that's humbly confident … The ease with which the four musicians commune is palpable.”
— Ron Schepper, Textura

“The sagacious guitarist from Maine is back … a mastery of hue and tone … he’s consolidated all his strengths into his most consistent effort yet.”

— S. Victor Aaron, Something Else!

"Spacious, slow-unfolding and modal in character, the record foregrounds Blotnick’s glistening guitar melodies … in a deep pocket rooted equally in jazz, rock and psychedelia. The album opens up slowly and rewards patience, built around quiet anthems and soundscapes that develop through small variations rather than overt climaxes."

— Caroline Bailey Erskine, NYS Music

“The album presents Blotnick working in a restrained, acoustic-centred setting, using spacious arrangements and slow-unfolding themes to foreground tone, harmonic detail and ensemble interplay … Improvisations develop through small variations rather than overt climaxes, giving the record a cohesive, contemplative character.”

— Bob Osborne, World of Jazz

BIOS

RYAN BLOTNICK (b. 1983) is an American guitarist and composer. He has been called “a vital contemporary voice” by Time Out New York, “engagingly pensive” by the New York Times, “an authentic, compelling player” by Cadence Magazine. His music is soulful, melodic, and a bit quirky. His studies in New York with '60s era masters like Gene Bertoncini, Harold Mabern, Yusef Lateef, Billy Taylor and Andrew Cyrille gave him a deep respect for the depth and breadth of jazz, and sparked a desire to contribute to its evolution. In Copenhagen (2002-2006), he attended the Rhythmic Music Conservatory, where young players like Jakob Anderskov, Jakob Bro and Kresten Osgood were trying to disrupt the city's cozy museum-jazz night clubs with vibrant and original sounds. Later, in New York, his interest in contemporary jazz led him to work with musical leaders like Michael Blake, Pete Robbins, Mat Maneri, Thomas Morgan and 2024 Pulitzer Prize-winning composer and multi-instrumentalist Tyshawn Sorey.

He now lives on Mount Desert Island in Maine, where he makes albums, plans tours, writes music for film, teaches at College of the Atlantic, and plays in a soul band, as well as original projects led by Phillip Greenlief and Danny Fisher-Lochhead. He hikes in Acadia National Park every day and occasionally leaves the island for groceries.

JEREMY VINER  (b. 1986, Ellsworth, ME) is a Berlin-based multi-instrumentalist, improviser, composer, and educator involved in a wide array of musical idioms. In 2023, after nearly 20 years in New York City, Viner moved to Berlin and continues to play an active role in both the New York and European experimental music scenes. His latest project is the collaborative trio SIFTERS, with Kate Gentile and Marc Ducret. As a saxophonist and clarinetist, Viner has performed internationally with ensembles led by John Hollenbeck, Steve Lehman, Tyshawn Sorey, Anna Webber, Kate Gentile, Rafiq Bhatia, and many others. Viner is a member of the genre-bending tenor saxophone quartet Battle Trance and the chamber minimalist ensemble Bing & Ruth, two of his longest-running musical collaborations. Jeremy Viner is a Vandoren Artist.

JOE SMITH studied at the Cincinnati Conservatory and the Manhattan School of Music with Vernel Fournier, Jimmy Lovelace, John Von Ohlen, John Riley, and Jeff Williams. From 1991 to 2000, he played in New York City and later lived in Barcelona. Under his own name he presented two albums at Fresh Sound Records, Happy and Melodic Workshop, with Bill McHenry, Gorka Benitez, Guillermo Klein, Chris Lightcap and Jorge Rossy. In addition, Smith was involved in recordings of John McNeil (This Way Out, 2002), Arthur Kell, Ryan Blotnick, Fredrik Carlquist, and Brandon Miller. In 2008, he founded the Asociación Libre Orkesta, a big band that combines improvised music with lyrics and picture projections. Smith appeared with the Orkesta at the Jazz al Parque Festival in Bogotá, Colombia in 2010.

Since 2011, he has been living in Berlin. His project, build-i-n-g features Liz Kosack on synthesizers and piano and Andrew D'Angelo on Alto Saxophone, mixing forward-moving rubato melodies and improvisations above pulse without meter grooves. His new trio with Bill McHenry and Masa Kamaguchi explores his compositions in a more straight ahead jazz setting. He can also be found playing with Johannes Hagge’s DRIFT, Larry Porter Trio, Jaume Llombard Sextet and Brandon Miller.

MATTHIAS PICHLER, born 1981, studied classical double bass at the Conservatory in Innsbruck, and jazz bass at the Anton Bruckner University in Linz. He received the Hans-Koller Award in 2004, which included a travel grant for a New York residence where he took lessons with John Patitucci, Larry Grenadier and Marc Johnson. In 2006, he gained the Hans-Koller Award in the category “Sideman of the year”, and was also nominated for the HK "Newcomer" Award the same year. In 2010, he won the first prize in the Jazz Competition of the international Double Bass Congress "Bass2010" in Berlin.

In 2014 and 2015 he was finalist of the New German Jazz Award. Matthias was a member of the Wolfgang Muthspiel Trio for 8 years, and played with many more internationally renowned musicians. Concerts with these artists brought him to over 30 countries all over the world. After moving to New York City, where he was living from 2017 to 2020, Matthias moved back to Berlin, where he is now part of various formations with a broad range of musical styles. Recently he started teaching at the wounderful JIMI/Tiroler Landeskonservatorium/Mozarteum Innsbruck.

Matthias was nominated for the Deutscher Jazz Preis 2025 in the category of string instruments and also won Album of the Year for his work on Peter Gall Quintet’s Love Avatar.

Linus Axelsson Quintet
description: Plays original music by Linus Axelsson. The music is influenced by  Berlins improvisation scene, where openness, risk and collective listening are at the center. The compositions function as starting points rather than ready-made templates. They provide direction, but leave room for improvisation, quick decisions. The music focuses on energy, interaction and presence rather than fixed forms.
